title: Counting-sort counting-loop execution
statement: Let $P$ be a program, let $d\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{lim}$ specify word, space, and depth limits, and take counting-sort parameters $A$, initial memory $\mu$, item and key functions $\mathrm{it},kf:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, and an initial state $\sigma$. Suppose the counting-sort preconditions hold. Suppose further that for some integer $\mathrm{entry}$, $\sigma$ is the state formed from the standard counting-sort argument frame with index $\mathrm{entry}$, arbitrary integer counter and place variables, and a memory $\mu'$ that agrees with $\mu$ outside the destination and counter intervals; moreover, every counter cell $\mathrm{cnt}+t$ for $t<\mathrm{nb}+1$ contains zero. Then the counting loop has an execution from $\sigma$ of cost at most $30n+6$ whose final state has index $n$, still agrees with $\mu$ outside those intervals, has counter cell $\mathrm{cnt}$ equal to zero, and has cell $\mathrm{cnt}+(t+1)$ equal to the number of indices $i<n$ with $kf(i)=t$ for every $t<\mathrm{nb}$.
hypotheses_covered: The initial state has the standard argument frame with index $\mathrm{entry}$ and arbitrary counter and place values
Initial memory agrees with $\mu$ outside destination and counter intervals
Every counter cell with offset $t<\mathrm{nb}+1$ is zero
